sections.heading: Product scope and release basis
sections.text: SunCore 5.0 is a 5 nm inference ASIC with PCIe Gen3 x4 host interface. This specification supports the planned release targeted for 2024-08-15; it is not evidence that production release has already occurred. The design envelope is 160 INT8 TOPS with a 28 W board design budget. Peak INT8 throughput is not sustained application throughput. Customers must validate their model, host bandwidth and thermal design. Engineering must retain the acceptance evidence for the exact silicon, firmware, driver and compiler configuration being released. Interface compatibility is evaluated against that configuration, not inferred from a shared product family name. This document controls the requirements and verification path; commercial allocation remains a separate process.

sections.heading: Interfaces, dependencies and use boundaries
sections.text: Capture frames on the host, prepare tensors, submit inference over PCIe, and return results to the host application. The qualification sequence is: Evaluate the reference board, confirm interface behavior, complete workload and thermal validation, then approve the production configuration. Agree the target workload, host interface, thermal boundary and qualification evidence before scheduling production adoption. The host owns capture, tensor preparation and the application response to inference results. The accelerator interface must reject malformed inputs rather than permit unbounded device activity. Customer model coverage is limited by the release operator list. A model that compiles successfully still needs application-level verification. Reference-board results do not establish customer-enclosure thermal performance. Production configuration changes must be reviewed for their effect on compatibility, power and the existing verification evidence.

sections.heading: Verification ownership and document navigation
sections.text: Riley Arden, VP Engineering owns engineering evidence; Quinn Mercer, Product Director owns the product acceptance boundary. The following requirements are grouped into host and compute behavior, fault handling and observability, then release and compatibility control. Each numbered requirement includes a concrete acceptance condition. The release checklist must identify the method, configuration and result for every control; a missing result is not an implied pass. Failures require corrective evidence before the release gate can close. Technical exclusions remain explicit: No regulatory certification, customer benchmark or customer endorsement is asserted.

sections.heading: 01 | Host link
sections.text: SC-5-01: Enumerate as a PCIe Gen3 x4 endpoint. Acceptance: Complete cold-boot enumeration on the reference host in 100 consecutive boots. Method: Reference-board verification. Evidence must identify the tested configuration and show the observed outcome, including any exception that prevents acceptance.

sections.heading: 02 | Arithmetic
sections.text: SC-5-02: Support signed INT8 multiply-accumulate inference. Acceptance: Match the published INT8 golden vectors exactly for supported operators. Method: Reference-board verification. Evidence must identify the tested configuration and show the observed outcome, including any exception that prevents acceptance.

sections.heading: 03 | Peak compute
sections.text: SC-5-03: Expose a peak of 160 INT8 TOPS at the rated clock. Acceptance: Check the architectural operation-count model against the rated configuration. Method: Reference-board verification. Evidence must identify the tested configuration and show the observed outcome, including any exception that prevents acceptance.

sections.heading: 04 | Power envelope

Evidence must identify the tested configuration and show the observed outcome, including any exception that prevents acceptance.

sections.heading: 05 | Model interface
sections.text: SC-5-05: Accept the release compiler's versioned binary model package. Acceptance: Load a package built with the matching toolchain and reject an incompatible major version. Method: Reference-board verification. Evidence must identify the tested configuration and show the observed outcome, including any exception that prevents acceptance.

sections.heading: Release gate and change control
sections.text: Acceptance requires all numbered controls to pass for the version-matched configuration. A functional pass cannot compensate for missing power or thermal evidence. Negative-path results must be retained alongside nominal-path results so that failure containment is auditable. Engineering and Product review interface-affecting changes before distributing a revised package. An unresolved compatibility issue blocks acceptance of the affected configuration rather than being carried silently into customer qualification. Customer-specific constraints remain outside a component-level claim of universal suitability. Request the version-matched evaluation kit and interface pack from applications@sunnysemi.example.
